notes: Checked own electric rates page (basic/demand/energy/FAC charges only, no TOU) and Reliable Power business page (no residential DR/thermostat program). SC-6 'Flex Rate' is an economic-development discount for large industrial customers tied to load factor/investment (not a TOU or shifting-oriented design), but per Mar 2026 GM interview the SC-6 agreements include a demand-response component for enrolled industrials -- tariff leaves 124-130 (SC-6 detail) not directly reviewed, so ci_dispatch sourced to trade-press interview not the tariff itself.

Current (12/1/25) rate sheet shows flat seasonal energy charges for residential (SC1/2) and flat demand+energy charges for large commercial/industrial (SC3/4) -- no TOU, no interruptible/curtailable rider. Energy Conservation page offers only efficiency rebates (appliance, heat pump, commercial, battery yard equipment) via NYMPA's Independent Energy Efficiency Program (IEEP), which is an MEUA/NYMPA-run efficiency program, not a TOU or utility-dispatched device program.

Rates page (residential non-heating/heating, small and large commercial) shows only flat seasonal block energy rates and a flat per-kW demand charge for Large Commercial -- no TOU, no interruptible/curtailable rider. Green Initiative page covers EV fleet, solar incentive, and efficient streetlighting pilots only -- no residential or C&I dispatch program found.

Residential rate is an inclining block (first/over 500 kWh) not TOU; Large Commercial has a flat per-kW demand charge, not a shifting-oriented design. However RVC's own 2024-2025 PSC energy-efficiency results report (Case 07-E-1303) describes a 'Residential and Small Commercial Demand Response Rebate': a utility-run DSM smart-thermostat program that is dispatched on curtailment event days (e.g. event called 7/16/2024, 158 customers, 0.3 MW curtailed) -- this is a true dispatch program covering both residential and small commercial customers, so both res_dispatch and ci_dispatch = Yes. HIFLD's ownership_type of 'NOT AVAILABLE' appears to be a data gap -- RVC's Electric Department is operated directly by the Village government, confirmed Municipal.

Reviewed PMLD's full DPS-filed tariff (PSC No. 1, all leaves): Residential (SC1), General Service non-demand (SC2), General Service demand-metered (SC4), Large General Service (SC6), and Private Outdoor Lighting (SC7). All rate designs are flat seasonal (winter/summer) energy and/or demand charges; SC6 sets on-peak hours (9am-10pm) only for measuring demand, not for differential pricing or dispatch. No TOU, CPP/PTR, interruptible/curtailable rider, or DR/dispatch program of any kind found in the tariff.
